evidence.text: The article cites oracle-bone examples Heji 71 and 32541 and Chu manuscript examples Xin 2.029 and Bao 2.95. It reviews a disputed interpretation of the central stroke as a sieve, while other cited accounts read the overall graph as scattered grain; it concludes that 米 referred broadly to dehusked grain rather than a single crop, later commonly specializing to rice. The account does not supply precise first-use dates or a complete semantic chronology.

Commons page yielded the exact original SVG image URL and public-domain claim for its modern redraw. A Xiaoxuetang character query URL failed; its landing page was inspected but did not provide a 米 record.

gaps: The exact Xiaoxuetang record for 米 was not retrieved, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.
The Commons original SVG URL was verified from the inspected description page, but the web viewer could not render the SVG; visual inspection is not claimed.
The exact historical date and inscription context for earliest semantic uses remain undetermined in these inspected materials; cited corpora references are not full artifact records.
The central stroke's interpretation remains disputed among sieve, stalk, or non-specific graphic separator; image candidate selection does not resolve the dispute.

items.period: Shang dynasty script style (image is a modern redraw)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 米 in Shang oracle-script style; the separated marks support the graph's traditional interpretation as scattered grain, while the middle stroke's referent remains disputed.
items.alt: Modern black-line vector drawing of the ancient character 米 in oracle-bone script style.
items.selection_reason: The Commons description page identifies the graph and style, gives its provenance and public-domain status, and the candidate illustrates the early graphic interpretation discussed in the scholarly source.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the file description page; modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

limitations.text: The viewer could not display the SVG, so the image's pixels were not visually inspected during research. The source identifies it as a modern redraw in Shang oracle-script style, not an artifact photograph.
The historical meaning of the central stroke is contested; the proposed candidate does not independently establish whether it depicts a sieve, stalk, or other feature.
